claims.text: MoNbTaW can be prepared as a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
Rapid quenching minimizes short-range chemical order in the baseline alloy.
Annealing at 800–1000 °C for controlled durations induces varying degrees of SRO in MoNbTaW.
The relevant structural mediator is the degree of short-range chemical order within the BCC matrix.
Inducing SRO produces localized lattice distortions.
SRO-associated localized lattice distortions impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion caused by SRO increases yield strength relative to a rapidly quenched baseline.
SRO-induced lattice distortion and altered phonon scattering modify the temperature dependence of the thermoelastic modulus.
Annealed samples with greater SRO will exhibit higher yield strength than the rapidly quenched baseline.
Annealed samples with greater SRO will exhibit a shifted, potentially increased, or otherwise modified temperature dependence of elastic modulus relative to the baseline.
Atom probe tomography and synchrotron X-ray diffraction can provide quantitative SRO metrics for this comparison.
A high-purity inert atmosphere can limit extrinsic environmental effects during annealing and high-temperature testing.
Annealing may also cause recovery or minor grain growth, which could independently affect the measured properties.
The proposed comparison uses rapid-quenched specimens as controls and annealed specimens as the intervention groups.
The hypothesis is falsified if directly measured SRO shows no systematic correlation with yield strength or thermoelastic-modulus changes relative to the baseline.
